cond_0001.intro:
The Niyogi lab at [Location masked] studies photosynthetic energy conversion and its regulation in algae and plants. The lab's long-term goals are to understand how photosynthesis works, how it is regulated, and how it might be improved to meet the world's needs for food and fuel. Current projects focus on mechanisms of photoprotection, assembly and dynamics of photosynthetic membranes, and improvement of photosynthesis, among others. By comparing how photosynthesis works in diverse organisms, the team hopes to uncover general design principles of natural photosynthesis as well as unique environmental adaptations.
As the Research Technician, you will support a senior research scientist and the lab manager with research projects involving genetics, molecular biology, biochemistry, spectroscopy, and light microscopy techniques. You will interact and collaborate with all team members in a diverse, collaborative lab environment. This is a good opportunity for someone who wants to gain additional hands-on research experience in a large, collaborative academic laboratory before moving on to graduate school.
Application Instructions: Please attach the following information (preferably as a single PDF document) as part of your application. Résumé/CV emphasizing prior experience. Cover letter outlining specific interest in this role and the Niyogi lab. Contact information for three references.
cond_0001.responsibilities:
Under the supervision of a senior lab scientist, you will support research projects involving genetics, molecular biology, biochemistry, spectroscopy, and confocal microscopy.
Maintain plants in growth chambers and greenhouse.
Culture microalgal and bacterial cells using sterile techniques.
Keep accurate laboratory records and communicate effectively and transparently about experiments.
Participate in weekly laboratory meetings and planning discussions.
Assist with other support duties relating to lab management and operations as required.
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
A bachelor's degree in molecular biology, biochemistry, biological sciences, or a closely related field.
At least one year of significant hands-on research experience (undergraduate coursework is acceptable).
Comfort and willingness to work with and handle plants, algae, and bacteria regularly.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills along with organizational and time management skills.
Strong attention to detail with the ability to maintain accurate records of experiments and procedures.
Able to manage multiple projects simultaneously and work well both independently and as part of a larger team.
Preferred Requirements

Research goals include understanding how photosynthesis works, how it is regulated, and how it might be improved to address global needs for food and fuel. Current projects focus on mechanisms of photoprotection, assembly and dynamics of photosynthetic membranes, and improvement of photosynthesis, among others. By comparing how photosynthesis works in diverse organisms, the team aims to uncover general design principles of natural photosynthesis as well as unique environmental adaptations.
In this role, you will support a senior research scientist and the lab manager with research projects involving genetics, molecular biology, biochemistry, spectroscopy, and light microscopy techniques. This is a good fit for someone who wants to build hands-on research experience in an academic laboratory before moving on to graduate school.
Application Instructions: Please attach the following information (preferably as a single PDF document) as part of your application. Résumé/CV emphasizing prior experience. Cover letter outlining specific interest in this role and the Niyogi lab. Contact information for three references.
cond_0025.responsibilities:
Under the supervision of a senior lab scientist, support research projects involving genetics, molecular biology, biochemistry, spectroscopy, and confocal microscopy.
Maintain plants in growth chambers and greenhouse.
Culture microalgal and bacterial cells using sterile techniques.
Keep accurate laboratory records and report on experiments clearly and directly.
Attend weekly laboratory meetings and contribute input to planning discussions.
Assist with other support duties relating to lab management and operations as required.
cond_0025.requirements:

A bachelor's degree in molecular biology, biochemistry, biological sciences, or a closely related field.

Comfort and willingness to work with and handle plants, algae, and bacteria.
Strong attention to detail with the ability to maintain accurate records of experiments and procedures.
Able to manage multiple projects simultaneously and work independently as well as within a larger team.
Able to meet deadlines and be self-motivated.
Preferred Requirements
Additional research/lab experience gained outside of school coursework.
Strong written communication and clear, direct verbal reporting, along with organizational and time management skills.
Proficient computer skills (PC and/or Mac, Microsoft Office Suite, etc.).
Eager to learn new techniques and expand scientific knowledge.

The long-term goal is to understand how photosynthesis works, how it is regulated, and how it might be improved to meet the world's needs for food and fuel. Current projects focus on mechanisms of photoprotection, assembly and dynamics of photosynthetic membranes, and improvement of photosynthesis, among others. By comparing how photosynthesis works in diverse organisms, the team hopes to uncover general design principles of natural photosynthesis as well as unique environmental adaptations.
As the Research Technician, you will regularly support a senior research scientist and the lab manager with research projects involving genetics, molecular biology, biochemistry, spectroscopy, and light microscopy techniques. A large part of the role is staying in contact with all team members and actively contributing to a diverse, collaborative lab environment. This is an ideal opportunity for someone who wishes to gain additional years of hands-on research experience in a large, highly collaborative academic laboratory before moving on to graduate school.

We are looking for a Research Technician to join the lab of Dr. Krishna Niyogi at [Location masked]. The lab studies photosynthetic energy conversion and its regulation in algae and plants. The long-term goal is to understand how photosynthesis works, how it is regulated, and how it might be improved to meet the world's needs for food and fuel. Current projects focus on mechanisms of photoprotection, assembly and dynamics of photosynthetic membranes, and improvement of photosynthesis, among others. By comparing how photosynthesis works in diverse organisms, the team hopes to uncover general design principles of natural photosynthesis as well as unique environmental adaptations.
As the Research Technician, you will support a senior research scientist and the lab manager with research projects involving genetics, molecular biology, biochemistry, spectroscopy, and light microscopy techniques. In this role you can interact positively and collaborate with all team members while working in a diverse, collaborative lab environment. This is an ideal opportunity for someone who wishes to gain additional years of hands-on research experience in a large, highly collaborative academic laboratory before moving on to graduate school. People who do well in this role are often quick to grasp the logic of molecular and biochemical work.
Application Instructions: Please attach the following information (preferably as a single PDF document) as part of your application. Résumé/CV emphasizing prior experience. Cover letter outlining specific interest in this role and the Niyogi lab. Contact information for three references.
cond_0202.responsibilities:
Under the supervision of a senior lab scientist, you will support research projects involving genetics, molecular biology, biochemistry, spectroscopy, and confocal microscopy.
Maintain plants in growth chambers and greenhouse.
Culture microalgal and bacterial cells using sterile techniques.
Keep accurate laboratory records and communicate effectively and transparently about experiments.
Participate in weekly laboratory meetings and planning discussions.
Assist with other support duties relating to lab management and operations as required.
cond_0202.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
A bachelor's degree in molecular biology, biochemistry, biological sciences, or a closely related field.
At least one year of significant hands-on research experience (undergraduate coursework is acceptable).
Comfort and willingness to work with and handle plants, algae, and bacteria regularly.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills along with organizational and time management skills.
Strong attention to detail with the ability to maintain accurate records of experiments and procedures.
Able to manage multiple projects simultaneously and work well both independently and part of a larger team.
Preferred Requirements
Additional research/lab experience gained outside of school coursework.
Proficient computer skills (PC and/or Mac, Microsoft Office Suite, etc.).
Able to work efficiently, meet deadlines, be adaptable, and be self-motivated.
Eager to learn new techniques and expand your scientific knowledge.

cond_0362.intro:
We are looking for a Research Technician to join our team. The lab studies photosynthetic energy conversion and its regulation in algae and plants. Long-term goals include understanding how photosynthesis works, how it is regulated, and how it might be improved to meet the world's needs for food and fuel. Current projects focus on mechanisms of photoprotection, assembly and dynamics of photosynthetic membranes, and improvement of photosynthesis, among others. By comparing how photosynthesis works in diverse organisms, the team hopes to uncover general design principles of natural photosynthesis as well as unique environmental adaptations.
As the Research Technician, you will support a senior research scientist and the lab manager with research projects involving genetics, molecular biology, biochemistry, spectroscopy, and light microscopy techniques. In this role you can interact positively and collaborate with all team members while working in a diverse, collaborative lab environment. This is an ideal opportunity for someone who wishes to gain additional years of hands-on research experience in a large, highly collaborative academic laboratory before moving on to graduate school.
Application Instructions: Please attach the following information (preferably as a single PDF document) as part of your application. Résumé/CV emphasizing prior experience. Cover letter outlining specific interest in this role and the Niyogi lab. Contact information for three references.
cond_0362.responsibilities:
Under the supervision of a senior lab scientist, you will support research projects involving genetics, molecular biology, biochemistry, spectroscopy, and confocal microscopy.
Maintain plants in growth chambers and greenhouse.
Culture microalgal and bacterial cells using sterile techniques.
Keep accurate laboratory records and communicate effectively and transparently about experiments.
Participate in weekly laboratory meetings and planning discussions.
Assist with other support duties relating to lab management and operations as required.
cond_0362.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in molecular biology, biochemistry, biological sciences, or a closely related field required; advanced degree strongly preferred.
At least one year of demonstrated hands-on research experience (undergraduate coursework is acceptable).
Proven track record of maintaining accurate records of experiments and procedures with strong attention to detail.
Solid understanding of sterile technique and comfort working regularly with plants, algae, and bacteria.
Exceptional verbal and written communication skills along with strong organizational and time management abilities.
Preferred Requirements
Substantial research or lab experience gained outside of school coursework.
Deep knowledge of managing multiple projects simultaneously, working well both independently and as part of a larger team.
Strong command of standard computer tools (PC and/or Mac, Microsoft Office Suite, etc.).
Demonstrated ability to work efficiently, meet deadlines, and adapt to changing priorities.
Proven eagerness to learn new techniques and expand scientific knowledge.
Physical Requirements
Remaining in a normal seated or standing position for extended periods of time; reaching and grasping by extending hand(s) or arm(s); dexterity to manipulate objects with fingers, for example using a keyboard; communication skills using the spoken word; ability to see and hear within normal parameters; ability to move about workspace. The position requires mobility, including the ability to move materials weighing up to several pounds (such as a laptop computer or tablet). Work may involve possible exposure to malodorous vapors, low dose radiation, contamination by toxic chemicals and acids and presence of carcinogenic substances or other hazardous materials.
Persons with disabilities may be able to perform the essential duties of this position with reasonable accommodation. Requests for reasonable accommodation will be evaluated on an individual basis.

We are looking for a Research Technician to join our team. The lab studies photosynthetic energy conversion and its regulation in algae and plants. The long-term goal is to understand how photosynthesis works, how it is regulated, and how it might be improved to meet the world's needs for food and fuel. Current projects focus on mechanisms of photoprotection, assembly and dynamics of photosynthetic membranes, and improvement of photosynthesis, among others. By comparing how photosynthesis works in diverse organisms, the team hopes to uncover general design principles of natural photosynthesis as well as unique environmental adaptations.
As the Research Technician, you will work alongside a senior research scientist and the lab manager on research projects involving genetics, molecular biology, biochemistry, spectroscopy, and light microscopy techniques. In this role you will collaborate with all team members in a diverse, cooperative lab environment. This is an ideal opportunity for someone who wishes to gain additional years of hands-on research experience in a large, collaborative academic laboratory before moving on to graduate school.

We are looking for a Research Technician to join our team. The lab studies photosynthetic energy conversion and its regulation in algae and plants. Long-term goals include understanding how photosynthesis works, how it is regulated, and how it might be improved to meet the world's needs for food and fuel. Current projects focus on mechanisms of photoprotection, assembly and dynamics of photosynthetic membranes, and improvement of photosynthesis, among others. By comparing how photosynthesis works in diverse organisms, the team hopes to uncover general design principles of natural photosynthesis as well as unique environmental adaptations.
As the Research Technician, you will support a senior research scientist and the lab manager with research projects involving genetics, molecular biology, biochemistry, spectroscopy, and light microscopy techniques. You will collaborate with all team members in a diverse, collaborative lab environment. This is an ideal opportunity for someone who wishes to gain additional years of hands-on research experience in a large, collaborative academic laboratory before moving on to graduate school.

cond_0475.intro:

Research goals include understanding how photosynthesis works, how it is regulated, and how it might be improved to address global needs for food and fuel. This is a good fit for someone who wants to build hands-on research experience in an academic laboratory before moving on to graduate school.
